title: Orchestration of staged shadowing and degraded compatibility handshakes
creator: Ayesha Patel
description:
Problem: We currently lack a robust orchestration layer that can run staged shadow traffic alongside canary slices while gracefully handling model variant incompatibilities across regions and capacity tiers. Team leads are seeing intermittent latencies and mismatch errors after canaries in low-capacity tiers, and there is no standardized degraded-compatibility handshake to let older model variants partially accept requests with reduced features.

Goal: Build an orchestration flow that allows: staged shadowing + canary slicing, dynamic compatibility negotiation (full | degraded | reject), region-aware failover, and automatic rollback when quality or latency SLOs breach thresholds. Must be cost-aware (avoid large shadow fanout in expensive tiers) and observable (per-slice metrics and compact post-canary report).

Out-of-scope for this ticket: model quantization, kernel selection, and persistent policy UI (Console work will be a follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Can launch a canary slice (0.5% - 10%) with shadow payloads routed to a shadow set without impacting production latency > 5th percentile SLA.
Compatibility negotiation API returns one of [full,degraded,reject] for each model pair; degraded handshakes allow partial response fields and defined schema markers.
Automatic rollback triggers when: 99th p50 latency increase > 30% for canary or error rate delta > 1.5% sustained for 5 minutes.
Region failover moves traffic to closest compatible tier within 120s with capacity-aware backoff and documented spillback behavior.
Cost control: shadow fanout per customer <= configured budget; system logs estimated incremental token cost before enabling large shadows.
End-to-end test harness simulating cross-region variant mismatch and tiered capacity shortage with deterministic outcomes.
implementation_steps: Design compatibility negotiation schema: handshake tokens and feature flags (schema in attachments).
Extend routing mesh to support: (a) staged canary weights, (b) shadow fanout routing, (c) per-slice cost caps.
Implement degraded-compatibility adapter that strips/marks unsupported fields and returns a compatibility header for downstream validation.
Add rollback evaluator service to aggregate canary metrics (latency quantiles, error delta, semantic-quality checks) and emit decisions with audit trail.
Wire region-aware failover layer to consult placement/capacity API and select nearest compatible tier; implement exponential backoff on spillbacks.
Create e2e integration tests and chaos scenarios (simulate GPU OOM, network partition between regions, and model-serving aborts).
Document migration plan and runbook for on-call engineers.
monitoring_and_alerting: Per-slice dashboards: request rate, token cost, 50/95/99 latency, infer error rate, compatibility-mode distribution.
Canary health alert: triggered when latency or error thresholds exceeded for 5 minutes; includes automated snapshot of recent traces.
Shadow cost alert: when estimated incremental spend for active shadows exceeds configured budget for a customer or org.
Rollback events are recorded in Audit logs and surfaced to Console with reason tags and before/after traffic topology.
rollback_conditions: Latency: 99th percentile increases by > 30% relative to baseline for the canary slice for 5 consecutive minutes.
Errors: absolute error rate increases by > 1.5% and relative increase > 100% compared to baseline for the same window.
Semantic-quality: automated evals on a fixed prompt set show drop in correctness/recall by > 6%.
Compatibility failure: > 0.5% of requests observed with missing required fields for the consuming application over 10 minutes.
Capacity spill: region failover causes downstream tier saturation leading to cascading throttles.
